plain_text:
The anticipation in the small room in
Culpeper, Virginia, was palpable as the
stylus touched down on a rare 100-year-old
wax cylinder recording. Chin in hand, film
producer Daniel Golding sat while his son,
Nate, stood behind him, hands in pocket.
semantic_text: The anticipation in the small room in Culpeper, Virginia, was palpable as the stylus touched down on a rare 100-year-old wax cylinder recording. Chin in hand, film producer Daniel Golding sat while his son, Nate, stood behind him, hands in pocket.

plain_text:
A scratchy sound emerged, followed by a
man's voice, which Golding identified as
his great-grandfather's. He was singing a
deer song in the language of the Quechans,
a Native American tribe indigenous to an
area along the Mexico border in Arizona and
California.
semantic_text: A scratchy sound emerged, followed by a man's voice, which Golding identified as his great-grandfather's. He was singing a deer song in the language of the Quechans, a Native American tribe indigenous to an area along the Mexico border in Arizona and California.

plain_text:
"My great-grandfather was the last one to
sing these songs," Golding said. "There's
nobody left in the community that sings
them."
semantic_text: "My great-grandfather was the last one to sing these songs," Golding said. "There's nobody left in the community that sings them."

plain_text:
Golding brought a film crew to the National
Audio-Visual Conservation Center (NAVCC)
in July 2022 to document a collaboration
between the Library and another tribe –
the Passamaquoddy of Maine – to recover
and share tribal language and cultural
practices from wax cylinder recordings in
the collections.
semantic_text: Golding brought a film crew to the National Audio-Visual Conservation Center (NAVCC) in July 2022 to document a collaboration between the Library and another tribe – the Passamaquoddy of Maine – to recover and share tribal language and cultural practices from wax cylinder recordings in the collections.

plain_text:
Golding's film, "Language Is Life," showcases
efforts by three Native communities - the
Passamaquoddy, the Cherokee and the
Navajo - to revitalize their languages and,
through language, to revive cultural heritage.
semantic_text: Golding's film, "Language Is Life," showcases efforts by three Native communities - the Passamaquoddy, the Cherokee and the Navajo - to revitalize their languages and, through language, to revive cultural heritage.

plain_text:
Narrated by Joy Harjo, the former U.S. poet
laureate, the film premiered at the Library
in November in advance of its broadcast as
one of four episodes in a PBS series,
"Native
America.
"
semantic_text: Narrated by Joy Harjo, the former U.S. poet laureate, the film premiered at the Library in November in advance of its broadcast as one of four episodes in a PBS series, "Native America. "

plain_text:
Anthropologist Jesse Walter Fewkes
documented Passamaquoddy folktales,
origin stories and vocabulary in 1890 using
wax cylinders, the recording medium of
the day. The 31 Passamaquoddy recordings
donated to the Library are the oldest
ethnographic field recordings known to
survive anywhere.
semantic_text: Anthropologist Jesse Walter Fewkes documented Passamaquoddy folktales, origin stories and vocabulary in 1890 using wax cylinders, the recording medium of the day. The 31 Passamaquoddy recordings donated to the Library are the oldest ethnographic field recordings known to survive anywhere.

plain_text:
The Library holds a total of about 9,000
turn-of-the-20th-century field recordings of
Native communities, the largest collection in
the U.S. Between 1977 and 1987, the Library's
American Folklife Center (AFC) transferred
these early field recordings to reel-to-reel
cassette tape as part of the Federal Cylinder
Project.
semantic_text: The Library holds a total of about 9,000 turn-of-the-20th-century field recordings of Native communities, the largest collection in the U.S. Between 1977 and 1987, the Library's American Folklife Center (AFC) transferred these early field recordings to reel-to-reel cassette tape as part of the Federal Cylinder Project.

plain_text:
Since 2015, using cutting-edge laser-
assisted technology, NAVCC has been
digitizing and restoring these recordings
through a project called Ancestral Voices –
semantic_text: Since 2015, using cutting-edge laser-assisted technology, NAVCC has been digitizing and restoring these recordings through a project called Ancestral Voices –

plain_text:
informally dubbed Federal Cylinder Project
2.0. Ancestral Voices is part of a larger
collaboration involving the AFC, Native
communities and other cultural institutions
to support revitalization of Native languages
and cultures.
semantic_text: informally dubbed Federal Cylinder Project 2.0. Ancestral Voices is part of a larger collaboration involving the AFC, Native communities and other cultural institutions to support revitalization of Native languages and cultures.

plain_text:
The task is urgent: According to “Language
is Life,” linguists predict that only 20 Native
languages will be spoken in North America
by 2050, down from more than 300 in 1492,
if language loss isn’t reversed.
semantic_text: The task is urgent: According to “Language is Life,” linguists predict that only 20 Native languages will be spoken in North America by 2050, down from more than 300 in 1492, if language loss isn’t reversed.

plain_text:
AFC is collaborating
with communities
to curate digitized
recordings and release
them selectively on
the Ancestral Voices
portal – communities
do not want all
materials shared
publicly. The folklife
center also provides
copies directly to
Native tribes.
semantic_text: AFC is collaborating with communities to curate digitized recordings and release them selectively on the Ancestral Voices portal – communities do not want all materials shared publicly. The folklife center also provides copies directly to Native tribes.

plain_text:
In recent years, for
example, it provided
the Warm Springs
Reservation in Oregon
with copies of out-of-
circulation recordings
that allowed the
community to
reincorporate content not used in 70 years
and Sioux communities with copies of
photographs and recordings that they said
documented the proper way to butcher
buffalo, an important cultural tradition.

plain_text:
When Golding heard the newly digitized
recording of his great-grandfather
in Culpeper in 2022, he immediately
recognized a big improvement over a
recording his parents had played for him in
the 1970s. The speed was corrected, and
the sound was much clearer.

plain_text:
For his son, Nate, then 16, the experience
was more profound – he had never heard
his great-great-grandfather's voice before.

plain_text:
“I hope these traditions are passed down
to the younger generation so the tradition
can live on,” Nate said, holding back tears.
“It gives me hope for our community to
become stronger. It just gives me hope in
my heart.”
